title: perfcheck names_successor still lets a dropped test excuse itself by its module stem or a call form of its name
goal: perfcheck's is_own matches a reason token against the dropped ids' own names by exact string, so the test module's stem (test_audit, for a dropped test of the test_audit module), or the test name written as a call (test_x()) or with trailing space inside the backticks, beside the live-module-calls-went-with phrase still counts as a successor. names_successor skips these forms of the dropped ids' own names too, and a genuine successor (a removed module's name) still counts.

run: import sys,tempfile; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import perfcheck; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); r=perfcheck.names_successor('live-module calls went with `test_audit`', ['_tools/test_audit.py::test_x'], d, ''); print(r); sys.exit(1 if r else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-yzs3bj6f review of BG-fiwxnug3. Planned 2026-11-10 in SP-u5zhszow; no sibling sprint holds _tools/perfcheck.py now (SP-3nqlr7b5's items do not touch it); the premise reproduces on origin/main: names_successor returns True for the stem form.
